headline: Dollar pauses near 19-month high as solid US spending meets AI jitters; rupee hits 7-month high
summary: The dollar index set a new 19-month high near 103.7 in Asia, then slipped about 0.1% to around 103.5 as Treasury yields eased with a 1% S&P 500 drop, even though strong retail sales and Musalem's call for several more hikes kept a December Fed hike fully priced. The rupee, peso and Taiwan dollar led on inflows, cheaper oil and central-bank support, while the franc and won lagged.
drivers: Fed hike bets stay locked in

October retail sales control group rose 0.6% against 0.3% expected and Musalem said several hikes may be needed by spring, so a December hike stays fully priced; the 10-year yield still eased to about 5.10% as stocks fell.
AI selloff deepens, then Nvidia beats

The Kospi fell 2.6% below 5,000 and the Taiex lost 948 points on foreign selling, pushing USD/TWD briefly through 33. After the bell Nvidia reported $115.8bn in revenue and guided to $130bn, lifting its shares about 2–4% after hours.
Taiwan's central bank turned the Taiwan dollar to a 32.85 close at the day's high, the PBOC fixed at 6.7132, and $6–7bn of recent portfolio inflows lifted the rupee 46 paise to 93.47.
view: Still bullish for the next 1–2 weeks, but the move is stretched, so I would add on dips rather than chase: the Fed is set to hike in December while the BoC and RBA look done, and I keep backing the dollar against the loonie, euro and Aussie. I fade it against the yen near 160 and now against the rupee on inflows. Nvidia's beat is the first test: a Nasdaq rebound that takes the DXY below 102.5, or FOMC minutes that cool talk of more hikes, would turn me neutral.
ideas: Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100 with the BoC on hold and the Fed hiking; for 1.4450, stop 1.4240.
Hold the short from 1.1170–1.1190 as the euro sits under 1.10; for 1.0900, stop 1.1060.
Hold the sale filled at 160.00–160.20 as Tokyo guards 160; for 157.50, stop 160.70.
review: No target or stop was hit: USD/CAD is about 210 pips in favour, EUR/USD and AUD/USD about 175 each, USD/JPY about 60 and USD/CHF and EUR/JPY about 25, so I hold them and trail the CHF and Aussie stops. The ringgit and rupiah longs are slightly ahead, USD/INR closed below its 93.50 floor and turns short, and all other ranges held, with USD/TWD's dip through 33 reversed by the close.

eurusd.note: Flat near 1.0995 after a new 19-month low of 1.0983; the short is about 180 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: The dollar paused rather than reversed. A stronger German ZEW (35.6 vs 29 expected) gave the euro no lift, while firm US retail sales (control group +0.6% vs +0.3%) and St. Louis Fed's Musalem calling for several more hikes kept the Fed's edge intact. The pair dipped under 1.10 again, but a slight narrowing in short-term rate gaps stopped a deeper break.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short for 1.0900 with the stop at 1.1060: the Fed is set to keep hiking past December while the ECB's next move after December is priced only for March. A close above 1.1060 would say the dollar's run has stalled.
eurusd.watch: Euro zone final CPI and Lagarde (Nov 18), FOMC minutes (Nov 18), euro zone flash PMIs (late Nov), ECB (Dec 17).

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces a late-cycle ECB.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.15% to near 1.3205, ending a five-day slide; mid-range in my 1.3150–1.3350 band.
gbpusd.why: Sterling did the moving, modestly. UK unemployment unexpectedly fell to 4.6% (4.7% expected) even as regular pay growth slowed to 3.5% and payrolls dropped 34,000, a mixed set that ING judged unlikely to derail BoE tightening. The pound dipped to 1.3169 early, then recovered as the dollar eased after US data.
gbpusd.outlook: I keep the 1.3150–1.3350 range: BoE hike bets offset a firm Fed. A UK CPI print well below the expected 3.7% would break 1.3150 and turn me bearish; a hot print would lift it toward 1.33.
gbpusd.watch: UK CPI and Bailey (Nov 18), UK retail sales (Nov 20), UK flash PMIs (late Nov), BoE (Dec 17).

view.call: 1.3150–1.3350; BoE hike bets vs firm Fed.

audusd.note: Steady near 0.6738 after a 10-month low of 0.6725; the sale is about 170 pips in favour.
audusd.why: Risk mood did the moving. The Aussie hit a new 10-month low in Asia as the Kospi and Taiex slid, then steadied as the dollar eased. RBA minutes showed six of nine members saw 4.85% as not clearly enough to tame inflation, a hawkish lean, but three dissenters warned of a sharper downturn, so traders still see no December hike.
audusd.outlook: I hold the sale for 0.6650, near the January lows BBH flags at 0.6660, and cut the stop to 0.6780. Nvidia's beat is the main risk: a close above 0.6780 on a tech rebound would end the call.
audusd.watch: Wage price index (Nov 18), jobs (Nov 19), Nvidia follow-through in Asia, monthly CPI (Nov 25).

view.call: Sale from 0.6900–0.6920; RBA divided, Fed hiking.

usdjpy.note: Flat near 159.48 after an Asian dip to 159.23; my sale from 160.00–160.20 is about 60 pips in favour.
usdjpy.why: The two forces cancelled out. Finance Minister Katayama repeated that Tokyo would act on one-sided moves in contact with the US Treasury, which kept traders from pushing through 160, while solid US retail sales and hawkish Fed talk supported the dollar. A 4bp fall in the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5.10% as stocks slid also helped the yen at the margin.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 157.50 with the stop at 160.70: words alone have capped the pair below 160 all month and a December BoJ hike is still in play. A close above 160.70 would show Tokyo is standing aside.
usdjpy.watch: FOMC minutes (Nov 18), Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments near 160, BoJ speakers, Japan's monthly intervention data (end-Nov).

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; Tokyo guards 160, BoJ may hike.

usdchf.note: Up about 0.25% to near 0.8417, a new 18-month high; my long is about 25 pips in favour.
usdchf.why: The dollar did the moving against a low-yielding franc. Musalem said several more Fed hikes may be needed by spring, while the SNB sits at 0%, so the franc keeps losing as a funding currency. Even with US stocks down again and Treasury yields slipping, the franc drew no haven demand.
usdchf.outlook: I hold the long for 0.8500 and raise the stop to 0.8360: the rate gap is widening and the franc is not acting as a haven. A close back below 0.8360 would say the breakout has failed.
usdchf.watch: FOMC minutes (Nov 18), Fed speakers, SNB comments, Swiss CPI (early Dec).

view.call: Long 0.8380–0.8400; rate gap, franc used to fund carry.

usdcad.note: Flat near 1.4300 after a 19-month high of 1.4316; the buy is about 210 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Both sides were quiet. The loonie got some help from a 0.8% rebound in Brent to $93.14 on tanker attacks in Hormuz and an extension of Canada-China trade deals, but Monday's tame CPI keeps the Bank of Canada on hold while the Fed hikes. Corpay noted the dollar looks stretched, which explains the pause near 1.43.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the buy for 1.4450 with the stop at 1.4240: the policy gap is the widest in this cycle. A sustained oil rally above $100 or a dovish Fed turn would be the main threats.
usdcad.watch: FOMC minutes (Nov 18), oil and Hormuz headlines, Canada retail sales (Nov 20).

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; tame CPI, BoC on hold, Fed hiking.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.666 offshore, near the strongest yuan level since early November.
usdcnh.why: The PBOC and summit hopes held it steady. The midpoint was set at 6.7132, the firmest since February 2023 but still about 420 pips weaker than the 6.6715 estimate, a sign Beijing is slowing gains rather than resisting the dollar. Traders also stayed long yuan into this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Xi and Trump are due to meet.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: steady but weak-side fixings lean against a faster rally while exporters sell dollars on bounces. A close below 6.64 after the summit would show Beijing is letting the yuan run.
usdcnh.watch: APEC summit and Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 18–19), loan prime rates (Nov 20), daily fixings vs estimates.

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slows the yuan, exporters sell USD.

usdhkd.note: Steady near 7.8466, about 35 pips from the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved it. The wide gap between US rates and HIBOR keeps the carry trade into US dollars attractive and holds the Hong Kong dollar near the weak end of its band. Tight interbank liquidity and the HKMA's 7.85 commitment cap the upside.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: carry keeps it pinned near 7.85, and only a HIBOR jump or HKMA buying at 7.85 would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, FOMC minutes (Nov 18).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Flat near 1.2884, inside my 1.2780–1.2920 range and just under 1.29.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving, gently. Fed hike bets kept USD/SGD firm, but UOB's S$NEER model shows the currency about 1.6% above the middle of the MAS band, which limits how far the Singapore dollar can fall against the basket. UOB sees 1.2900 as a cap for now, with strong support near 1.2840.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range: the MAS band anchors the Singapore dollar while a hiking Fed keeps the pair heavy. A close above 1.2920 would open 1.3000.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore final Q3 GDP (late Nov), FOMC minutes (Nov 18), Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won fell 2.5 to 1,338.2 in Seoul as the Kospi lost 2.6% to below 5,000; offshore near 1,335.
usdkrw.why: Equity outflows did the moving. Foreigners sold a net 1.45 trillion won of Korean shares, pushing the Kospi to 4,968.5, its first close under 5,000 since February, and their dollar buying briefly took the pair toward 1,340. Exporters' dollar sales near those levels and a steady dollar index around 103.5 limited the damage.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling caps the pair, while foreign stock selling and Fed hikes limit won gains. Nvidia's beat could ease outflows; a Seoul close below 1,325 would open 1,315, above 1,365 would revive the long.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows after Nvidia, FOMC minutes (Nov 18), oil, Korea November exports (Dec 1).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar rose 3.6 cents to 32.850 in Taipei, the session high, after touching 33.015.
usdtwd.why: The central bank did the moving. Foreign investors sold another NT$38.1bn of shares and the Taiex lost 948 points to 40,092, which pushed the pair through 33 in the morning. Exporters sold dollars near 33 and local reports said the central bank stepped in again late in the day, turning a 12-cent loss into a gain.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are clearly defending 33 and exporters see it as a selling point, but foreign outflows cap the Taiwan dollar. A close above 33.05 would show the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows after Nvidia, index futures settlement (Nov 18), central bank action near 33.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit flat at 4.0915/0960 at the 6pm KL close, trading 4.0892–4.0945; my long is slightly ahead.
usdmyr.why: Neither side moved much. Bank Muamalat's chief economist said caution over the tech selloff and US-China trade tensions kept the pair in a narrow range, while bets on more aggressive Fed tightening kept dollar demand steady. The ringgit eased against most other majors and ASEAN peers.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the long for 4.125 with the stop at 4.075: Fed hikes outweigh Bank Negara's steady rate for now. A close back below 4.075, perhaps on a tech rebound, would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia October CPI (late Nov), regional chip stocks after Nvidia, oil, FOMC minutes (Nov 18).

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; break of 4.085 on Fed hike bets.

usdphp.note: Peso rose 27 centavos to 63.67 at the BAP close, ending a four-day slide after testing 63.99.
usdphp.why: Oil and profit-taking did the moving. RCBC's Ricafort pointed to crude near 2.5-month lows and the resulting cut in local pump prices, which eases the import bill. Traders took profit on dollar longs after the pair retested the highs just below 64, and volume rose to $1.49bn.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: lower oil, holiday remittances and possible BSP hikes help, but the Fed weighs. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: Oil and Hormuz headlines, BSP comments, FOMC minutes (Nov 18), BSP decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; oil, remittances and BSP vs Fed.

usdidr.note: Rupiah edged up 12 points to 18,256 spot, but JISDOR set a record weak 18,264. Long about 30 points up.
usdidr.why: Positioning before Bank Indonesia did the moving. Spot steadied off Monday's record low as traders waited for BI's decision, where analysts expect a fifth straight hold, while the JISDOR reference rate still slipped to a record. High US Treasury yields and Fed hike bets keep the pressure on.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long for 18,500 with the stop at 18,150: Fed bets, MSCI-related outflows and politics outweigh BI's smoothing. A surprise BI hike that pulls the rupiah below 18,150 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia decision (Nov 18), MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, FOMC minutes (Nov 18).

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; Fed, politics and outflows vs BI.

usdinr.note: Rupee rose 46 paise to 93.47, its strongest close since April, breaking below my 93.50 range floor.
usdinr.why: Flows did the moving. Foreign portfolio investors have brought in roughly $6–7bn in about two weeks, a Bank of Baroda treasurer said, and local stocks rose. Brent, down about 20% this month to near $93, cuts importers' dollar needs; the rupee is up about 1.6% in November, its best month since March 2025.
usdinr.outlook: The close below 93.50 turns me short USD/INR toward 93.00 with a stop at 93.80: inflows and lower oil are doing the work. RBI dollar buying to rebuild reserves is the main risk; a close above 93.80 would end the call.
usdinr.watch: Foreign equity flows, oil and Hormuz headlines, India flash PMIs (late Nov), RBI decision (Dec 4).

view.call: Sell 93.50–93.60; FPI inflows and cheaper oil.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 175.35, below the old 175.5 range floor; my sale is about 25 pips in favour.
eurjpy.why: Both legs were steady. The euro held near its 19-month low against the dollar despite a strong ZEW, and the yen stayed firm on Tokyo's warnings near 160. With both currencies flat against the dollar, the cross drifted just under 175.5.
eurjpy.outlook: I hold the sale for 174.0 with the stop at 176.3: the euro is losing ground and the yen is protected near 160. A close back above 176.3 would say the old range has resumed.
eurjpy.watch: Lagarde and euro zone CPI (Nov 18), Japan CPI (Nov 20), Tokyo comments, euro zone PMIs (late Nov).

view.call: Sell 175.4–175.8; weak euro, yen guarded near 160.

cnhjpy.note: Little changed near 23.92, in the upper half of my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: Neither side moved. The yuan held near a two-week high against the dollar on a firm PBOC fixing and summit hopes, and USD/JPY was flat below 160, so the cross barely changed. Both currencies are anchored by officials: Beijing slows the yuan, Tokyo caps the yen's losses.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the cross follows USD/JPY, which Tokyo is likely to cap near 160. A close above 24.2 would show intervention is not coming.
cnhjpy.watch: APEC Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 18–19), PBOC fixings, Japan CPI (Nov 20).

view.call: 23.6–24.2; yen near Tokyo's line, yuan held.

eurcnh.note: Little changed near 7.33, mid-way in my 7.28–7.40 range.
eurcnh.why: Neither side moved much. The euro held near its 19-month low against the dollar, and the yuan stayed firm on a strong-for-the-year PBOC fixing and APEC summit hopes. With both legs flat against the dollar, the cross went sideways.
eurcnh.outlook: I keep a 7.28–7.40 range with a downward tilt: euro weakness should continue, while the PBOC slows yuan gains. A close below 7.28 would open 7.22.
eurcnh.watch: APEC summit (Nov 18–19), PBOC fixings, Lagarde (Nov 18), euro zone PMIs (late Nov).

view.call: 7.28–7.40; weak euro vs PBOC brake on yuan.

watch: Next: FOMC minutes, UK CPI, Bank Indonesia, Lagarde and Australian wages (Nov 18), the APEC Xi-Trump meeting (Nov 18–19), Australia jobs (Nov 19), Japan CPI and China's loan prime rates (Nov 20), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and ECB, BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo's 160 line and Taiwan's defence of 33.
